h: New Town, New Ways to Win
p: Stevenage has a special place in British history as the first of the post-war new towns. It was designated in 1946 as part of a plan to rehouse people from London, and it was built with a pedestrianised town centre that was one of the first of its kind. That forward-thinking spirit lives on in the town's mix of modern venues and old-fashioned charm in the Old Town.

Getting here is straightforward. Stevenage station sits right by the town centre, with fast trains to London King's Cross and Cambridge, so it's a handy spot for groups coming from different directions. If you're driving, the A1(M) runs alongside the town, with car parks around the centre.

For the best evening, plan ahead. Decide on your games, mix up the teams and make sure everyone knows when to arrive. If it's a celebration, a few prizes and forfeits can add to the fun. Games bars are a good choice for groups with mixed interests, as there's something for everyone.

With extra time, the Old Town High Street is a pleasant change from the modern centre, with historic buildings, pubs and places to eat. Stevenage is also known as the hometown of Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton, which adds a bit of competitive spirit to the place. Further afield, Hatfield House, the childhood home of Elizabeth I, is a short drive south, and the Shaw's Corner house of playwright George Bernard Shaw is nearby too.
